summary: The note covers the Neighborhood Cleanup Drive held in Springdale on September 10, 2023, which drew over 300 volunteers. It traces the effort to retired teacher Maria Gonzalez, who founded the Greening Springdale Committee after seeing litter harm ducks in a pond. It describes the planning, youth involvement, business and official support, community bonding, and plans for future events.
one_line: Over 300 Springdale residents joined a September 2023 neighborhood cleanup led by the Greening Springdale Committee, which is now planning future events.
key_facts: The Neighborhood Cleanup Drive took place on September 10, 2023, in Springdale.
Over 300 volunteers took part, including families with young children, teenagers, and senior citizens, starting at Springdale Park.
Maria Gonzalez, a retired school teacher and longtime resident, started the movement after seeing a family of ducks wading through plastic bags and soda cans in the pond.
Gonzalez's outreach to neighbors and the Springdale Community Association led to the Greening Springdale Committee, which organized the first cleanup two years earlier.
The Greening Springdale Committee is now cochaired by Maria Gonzalez and local entrepreneur Rajiv Singh.
Committee members met weekly before the event, distributing flyers, organizing fundraisers, and encouraging local schools to join the educational campaign.
Local businesses sponsored safety vests, gloves, and recycle bags; a local grocery chain donated reusable water bottles.
Jaime Lee, the Community Association President, led the opening ceremony.
Samantha Patel, a high school senior and president of the Eco Warriors Club, led students in the cleanup and in educational workshops for younger children.
Restaurants offered discounts to volunteers, hardware stores provided tools and materials, and several council members joined the cleanup.
Councilwoman Angela Roberts handed out certificates of appreciation to the volunteers.
David O'Connor, a recent transplant, said he met more neighbors that day than in the two years he had lived in Springdale.
The event inspired similar initiatives in adjacent neighborhoods and encouraged sustained commitment to recycling and waste reduction.
The committee is planning future events, including monthly mini-cleanups and partnerships with schools for ongoing education programs.
